error_directions.220: forgets the 30 donated liters: 210/0.75=280, minus 60 = 220; below key; stem names the add-on, so a student cannot rely on predicting it
error_directions.120: multiplies by 0.75 instead of dividing: 240*0.75=180, minus 60 = 120; below key; a student who knows dividing by a number under 1 makes it bigger could predict this side
error_directions.250: unclear path (e.g. 280-30 = 250, subtracting the liters from bottles, or arithmetic slip); below key; not predictable

MM5-N18.extreme_single_bound: bottles before giveaway > 240 (dividing by <1), so answer > 180
MM5-N18.interior_parity: 220 and 250: both plain whole numbers of the same form; key is not interior
MM5-N18.grade_note: 6.NS.3 multi-digit decimal division in a 3-step context; about half of grade 6 would get it
MM5-N18.note: (210+30)/0.75 = 320; 320-60 = 260. Key is the largest option and the common errors (forget 30, multiply by 0.75) fall below, but the 30-forgetting error is not readable as a direction from the stem alone; backward check (x+60)*0.75=240 is possible but options ascending reach the key on the 4th try.

MM5-N01.free_elimination: estimate: 7 bags each over 1.1 kg is over 7.7 kg, plus 2.15 is over 9.85, so 9.30 is too small

error_directions.9.30: treats 7 x 1.15 as 7.15 (multiplies only the whole part): 7.15+2.15 = 9.30; below key; predictable that partial-product errors go low
error_directions.10.10: 7 x 1.15 slipped to 7.95 (7 x 0.15 written as 0.95): 7.95+2.15 = 10.10; below key; not readable from stem
error_directions.9.90: 7 x 1.15 slipped to 7.75 (e.g. 0.75 for 7 x 0.15 dropping the carried 1): 7.75+2.15 = 9.90; below key; not readable from stem

MM5-N01.interior_parity: 9.90 and 10.10: same form, both two-decimal amounts; key is not interior
MM5-N01.arith_tell: fractional part alone decides: 7 x 0.15 = 1.05 -> .05, + .15 = .20, and 10.20 is the only option with tenths digit 2 (cheaper than the full product but still a computation)
MM5-N01.grade_note: 5.NBT.7 decimal times whole number plus a decimal addend, two steps; most grade 5 students get it
MM5-N01.note: 7 x 1.15 = 8.05; 8.05 + 2.15 = 10.20. Key is the largest option; all distractors are under-multiplication slips, but a student cannot read from the stem that errors go low.

MM5-N11.free_elimination: 10 drains of 3/8 gallon is clearly more than 3 gallons, far more than the 1 1/2 poured back, so the tank ends below its starting 9 3/8; 9 5/8 is above the start

error_directions.7 7/8: treats 10 x 3/8 as 3 gallons: 9 3/8 - 3 + 1 1/2 = 7 7/8; above key; not readable from stem
error_directions.7 3/8: regroups 9 3/8 as 8 13/8 (borrowing ten): 8 13/8 - 3 6/8 = 5 7/8, + 1 1/2 = 7 3/8; above key; not readable from stem
error_directions.9 5/8: no clear computation path; above key and above start; struck by direction of net change

MM5-N11.interior_parity: 7 3/8 and 7 7/8: same mixed-number form; key is not interior
MM5-N11.grade_note: 5.NF.4 fraction x whole plus mixed-number subtraction with regrouping and addition with unlike denominators; three steps, harder end of grade 5
MM5-N11.note: 10 x 3/8 = 30/8 = 3 6/8; 9 3/8 - 3 6/8 = 5 5/8; + 1 4/8 = 7 1/8. Key is smallest and both computable errors fall above it, but the stem does not signal that errors go high.

error_directions.14.30: rounds 3.95 down to 3.90 (the intended trap): 6.20+2.60+3.90+1.60 = 14.30; below key; not readable from stem
error_directions.14.70: rounds every price up to the next ten cents: 6.30+2.70+4.00+1.70 = 14.70; above key; not readable
error_directions.14.60: mixed rounding slips (e.g. 2.63 and 1.61 rounded up); above key; not readable

MM5-N06.interior_parity: 14.40 and 14.60: same form; the key is the interior value nearest the exact total 14.43, but neither is cleaner
MM5-N06.grade_note: 5.NBT.4 rounding decimals to tenths and adding; the 3.95 -> 4.00 carry is the discriminator, roughly half of grade 5
MM5-N06.note: 6.20+2.60+4.00+1.60 = 14.40. Shortcut: the exact sum 14.43 rounded to the nearest ten cents also gives 14.40, so a student who skips the per-item rounding and the 3.95 trap still lands on the key; this weakens the item's measurement of the rounding skill (requires adding, so not free).
